newsitem.title: CANADA: CANADIAN BONDS CLOSE WEAKER, BUT OUTPERFORM U.S..
newsitem.headline: CANADIAN BONDS CLOSE WEAKER, BUT OUTPERFORM U.S..

text.p: Canadian bonds closed weaker in moderate trade on Thursday, pulled lower by a late downturn in U.S. Treasury prices, analysts said.

"The U.S. market collapsed and it dragged us along with it. We actually have done relatively well against the U.S.," said David Yu, fixed-income portfolio manager with Perigee Investment. "I think some people were surprised with the market behaviour in the U.S. There's really no particular logic behind it."
Canada's 30-year benchmark bond fell C$0.17 to C$120.25 to yield 6.459 percent.
The U.S. 30-year bond fell 18/32 to yield 6.52 percent. The negative spread between the bonds widened to six basis points from three basis points at Wednesday's close.

Canadian bonds traded stronger for much of the session but weakened with U.S. Treasuries shortly after the release of the U.S. 30-year bond auction. While the auction reflected decent interest, analysts said a lack of follow through buying and profit taking pushed the market through key support levels.
Canadian fixed-income investors are now looking ahead to the release of the key Canadian employment report for July out tomorrow.
Yu noted there is speculation that a stronger-than-expected Canadian report could prompt the Bank of Canada to hike interest rates for the second time this year.
In other prices, Canada's 10-year benchmark bond fell C$0.14 to C$109.46 to yield 5.960 percent. The U.S. 10-year bond fell 10/32 to yield 6.24 percent.
The negative spread between the bonds widened to 28 basis points from 27 basis points at Wednesday's close.
